summary: Same idea — saturated-hue horizontal/vertical 1-px 'street' bars drawn on black — but the port draws far too many, far too thick, and its bars almost never expire, so the grid saturates into a near-frozen plaid instead of the original's sparse, constantly-turning-over traffic.
observations: Both sides expose the identical control surface: sliderLineWidth, sliderLineSpeed, sliderColorSpeed, all kind 'slider'. No control-surface mismatch.

Shared vocabulary is right: both draw axis-aligned single-colour bars (some horizontal, some vertical, of varying length) on a pure-black field, in fully-saturated spectrum hues that shift over time. A viewer would recognise the family.

DENSITY: at untouched defaults on the 16x16 default rig, orig meanBrightness avg 5 (max 9) vs port 18.4 (max 36); over the 60 s survey orig 5 vs port 27. Contact sheets show orig holding ~2-6 bars on screen at any moment for the whole 60 s, while the port packs 15-25.

DENSITY, exact: --dump on a 48x48 re-render at LineWidth=0.5/LineSpeed=0.5/ColorSpeed=0.5 (label grid48-dump, t=22 s) gives orig 490/2304 pixels lit (21.3%) vs port 2017/2304 (87.5%) — the port is very nearly a solid field.

THICKNESS: orig bars are exactly 1 px wide at every setting and every grid size measured (16x16 dumps at LineWidth 0/0.5/1; 48x48 dump). Port bars are 2 px at 16x16 and ~3 px at 48x48 untouched/mid-dial — so port thickness scales with the grid while the original's does not (resolution-dependence mismatch, checked at --grid 16x16 and --grid 48x48).

PERSISTENCE/MOTION is the biggest gap: orig-motion.png filmstrips (12 consecutive frames, 0.55 s) show the original's bars visibly growing, retracting and being wholly replaced — one full scene turnover inside that half-second. The port's filmstrip over the identical frames is essentially a still image repeated 12 times.

Whole-window rhythm images say the same thing over 12 s (ctl-width-0.5): the original's rhythm is dense short-lived colour blocks — everything transient; the port's is unbroken vertical stripes running the full height of the window with only slow colour drift, i.e. bars that are placed once and never removed.

With ColorSpeed forced to 0 (ctl-color-0, LineSpeed 0.5), the port's contact sheet from t=20 s to t=31.9 s is near-identical cell to cell — with colour animation removed there is almost no remaining animation at all. The original turns its scene over completely between every one of those cells.

motion stat across the LineSpeed sweep (LineWidth 0.5, ColorSpeed 0.5, skip 20, 12 s @20 fps): orig 2 / 3 / 5 / 14 at LineSpeed 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 1; port 1 / 1 / 1 / 9. The port only starts turning bars over near LineSpeed 1, where the original is already at ~3x that motion. motionLit at untouched defaults: orig avg 15.1, port avg 5.0.

Startup: the port begins black and ACCUMULATES to its saturated state over the first ~2-3 s and then stays saturated (confirmed at --skip 100: orig sparse, port still packed, meanBrightness 5 vs 23). The original has no such fill-up transient — it is sparse from the first bar onward and stays sparse for the whole 60 s survey.

sliderLineWidth=0 renders the original completely black (0 lit pixels at t=25 s) — no bars at all — while the port still draws a full set of 1-px bars (52 lit pixels). The port floors the width instead of extinguishing the pattern.
Not a seed fluke: seed 1234 at the same dialed settings reproduces the same split (orig mean 11 / motion 5, port mean 45 / motion 1).
Both sides: wantsSensors false, no compile or runtime errors, no harness warnings.

dials.name: sliderLineWidth
dials.origEffect: Acts as a density/enable knob, not a thickness knob: at 0 the grid is entirely black, at 0.5 ~5 bars are present (53/256 px lit), at 1 ~9 bars (89/256 px lit). Bar thickness stays 1 px throughout.
dials.portEffect: Acts as both density AND thickness, and never turns off: at 0 it still draws a full set of 1-px bars (52/256 lit), at 0.5 it fills 178/256 (70%) with 2-px bars, at 1 it fills 226/256 (88%). Direction of change is right; magnitude and floor are wrong.

dials.name: sliderLineSpeed
dials.origEffect: Sets bar turnover/growth rate; motion stat rises 2 -> 3 -> 5 -> 14 across 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 1 while mean brightness stays flat at ~11-12, i.e. faster churn at constant on-screen density.
dials.portEffect: Same direction but far weaker and coupled to density: motion 1 / 1 / 1 / 9 across the same values, and mean brightness falls 49 -> 48 -> 37 -> 35 as speed rises, i.e. the port only clears its backlog by running fast. At 0-0.5 the port is visually frozen.

dials.name: sliderColorSpeed
dials.origEffect: Rate of hue change on the bars; motion 5 at 0 vs 7 at 1 with brightness unchanged (12 both). Small effect because the original's motion is dominated by bar turnover.
dials.portEffect: Same character (hue-change rate, motion 1 at 0 vs 3 at 1, brightness 38 both) but it carries almost all of the port's visible animation: with ColorSpeed=0 the port is nearly a still frame over 12 s.

feedback: Cut on-screen bar density by roughly 4-5x. On the 16x16 default rig at mid dials the original holds ~5 bars / ~20% of pixels lit; the port holds ~15-20 bars / ~70%. On 48x48 the gap is 21% lit vs 87% lit.

Bars must be exactly 1 pixel wide, at every LineWidth setting and every grid size. The port draws 2 px at 16x16 and ~3 px at 48x48 — its width is being computed as a fraction of the grid; the original's is a fixed 1 px.

Give bars a finite lifetime. The original replaces its entire on-screen set roughly every half second at LineSpeed=0.5; the port's bars persist for the whole 12 s window and only their colour changes. This is the single most visible difference: the port reads as a static plaid wallpaper, the original as flowing traffic.

Decouple density from LineSpeed. In the original, raising LineSpeed speeds up turnover while on-screen density stays constant (mean brightness ~11-12 at every speed). In the port, density is a backlog that only drains at high speed (mean 49 at speed 0 down to 35 at speed 1).
LineWidth=0 should extinguish the pattern entirely (the original renders a fully black grid there). The port floors the width at 1 px and keeps drawing.
Remove the fill-up transient: the port starts black and takes ~2-3 s to reach its (over-)saturated steady state. The original is at its steady density from the first bars onward.
Bar LENGTHS should vary — the original draws partial runs (e.g. 8, 10, 16 and 27 px long on a 48-wide row) as well as full spans. Port bars are mostly full-span, which contributes to the solid look.
Palette and hue behaviour need no work: saturated full-spectrum hues on black, and the ColorSpeed response matches in character and direction.
